PI Commercial Single-Engine Checkride Prep - Slow flight - SAT * I gave some grace on this for airspeed because it was slightly bumpy and our airspeed had been bouncing around 4 knots however you were pretty stable Chandelle - SAT Power On - SAT *use a bit more right rudder during the stalled condition, you got 9 degrees off heading. I demonstrated the amount of pitch down and when to start that pitch up (64KIAS). Keep it smooth. It’ll never give you a secondary horn. Steep turns - UNSAT *We blew through the airspeed, altitude and heading. You didn’t have enough power added in on the roll so adding back pressure we got into the 70s on airspeed. To rebuild the airspeed you pitched down, we lost altitude. And because you were focused on this you banked right past your heading. It’s a domino effect, if you know it’s UNSAT, recover, admit to the recognition and set back up. Lazy 8s - UNSAT *got off the heading and busted the airspeed and altitude. PI Commercial Duties-of-PIC Night - We went to Chattanooga to do the night landings. - Stayed ahead of the plane by completing the appropriate checklists. - Try finding the airport beacon and that will help you find the location of where the airport is. - When ATC gives you a traffic alert and you find traffic, you need to let ATC know you have traffic in sight. - Nice landings tonight.

PI Commercial Single-Engine Training - Soft field takeoff: Speed up to 64 or 76 KIAS but nice job staying in ground effect. - Chandelle: SAT. Nice job staying coordinated and ending the maneuver just above stall speed. - Lazy eights: SAT. Start pitching up when you are getting close to the altitude (the one you started the maneuver at) - Accelerated stall: Recover on the first indication which is most likely the stall horn. Good recovery. - Steep spirals: Watch the altitude you start at and end. Nice job banking steeper with a tailwind and banking shallower with a headwind. - Eights on pylon: Nice job waiting to find two pylons. Make sure you are keeping the same bank and changing the pitch. You change groundspeed with pitch and not power. - Soft field landing: UNSAT - rounded out too early and entered ground effect to high. SAT - much better - Short field landing: UNSAT. You chose the second strip to be your landing point which means you need to move up your aiming point to the start of the runway or even the grass.

PI Power-Off 180° Practice - Power off 180 practice at KJZP! - When performing power off approaches the most important thing to understand is the direction and strength of the wind and its effect on your ground speed and track. Power off 180s are not too tricky when winds are calm. My goal is to have you be able to truly asses what is going on during the maneuver and make the proper decision when it comes to managing the airplane energy/winds/etc! - Good job completing the before landing checklist in its entirety before every landing and before a beam our touch down point ofthe thousand footers. - Once a beam we went power idol. pitching for 76 starting our base once we lose roughtly 100' from TPA. - I LOVE  they way you talk through your thought process and asseing the situation. Continue to talk out loud. " Am I high? Am I low? Am i Fast Am I slow?" - If we are high we have options... extend our ground track, add flaps, slip. - Power off 180 - just a hair long. Came in a little fast caused us to float. - Power off 180 - a little long again. - Power off 180 - little short - Power off 180 - little short - Power off 180 - SAT - Power off 180 - SAT - pwer off 180- balloned up slightly. just watch you pitch. So you dont pull back to agreesive. - Back to KPDK! Good job today, your last few power off 180s were better. What I like to see if by the end of the flight youre really taking your time and making decisions based off what youre seeing and not what you think! - We'll be sure to do at least one power off 180 every flight in your checkride prep so that you continue having practice in different conditions!
